bibl.title: Hippocampal Sequences During Exploration: Mechanisms and Functions

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: possible mechanisms and functions of hippocampal theta sequences during exploration
span.quote: The present review discusses possible mechanisms and functions of hippocampal theta sequences during exploration. We present several lines of evidence suggesting that these neural sequences play a key role in information processing and support the formation of initial memory traces, and discuss potential functional distinctions between neural sequences emerging during theta vs. awake sharp-wave ripples.

span.label: whether phase precession is a cause or a consequence of the formation of theta sequences
span.quote: Whether phase precession is a cause or a consequence of the formation of theta sequences remains unresolved. As discussed above, phase precession could result from a variety of mechanisms that do not require sequential connectivity between neighboring place cells ( detuned oscillators and somato-dendritic interference models). Independent initiation of phase precession in successive cells would automatically yield theta sequences (Skaggs et al., 1996 ). Thus, phase precession would be a causal mechanism of theta sequences. An alternative view is that hippocampal sequences result from specific patterns of connectivity within the hippocampal network ( network connectivity models; see also Dragoi and Tonegawa, 2011 ). At the single cell level, this would be manifested as phase precessing spikes. Thus, phase precession would be a consequence of the formation of theta sequences.

span.label: a closer examination of the available data suggests a more complex picture, and the review points out the current inconsistencies and overlooked findings
span.quote: As it turns out, a closer examination of the available data suggests a more complex picture. Below, we point out some of the current inconsistencies and overlooked findings.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: This indicates that theta sequences play a causal role in establishing initial memory traces, which can later be reinstated during sleep for memory consolidation.

span.label: hippocampal theta sequences
span.quote: These sequences are known as “theta sequences.”

span.label: review
span.quote: The present review discusses possible mechanisms and functions of hippocampal theta sequences during exploration.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: theta cycles compress spikes of successive place-cell assemblies into windows short enough for Hebbian synaptic plasticity, which is how an initial memory trace gets stored
span.quote: Theta sequences chunk information into time windows conducive to classical synaptic plasticity mechanisms, and appear to support the initial storage of memory traces.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: repeated theta-compressed activation of successive place cells induces asymmetric synaptic connectivity, and that stored asymmetry is what allows the same trajectory to be replayed offline during sleep
span.quote: A possible solution would be that once theta sequences emerge due to independent phase precession, the repeated activation of successive neurons induces synaptic changes that result in asymmetric network connectivity; this would allow trajectory replay during sleep (Drieu et al., 2018 ; see section 3.3).

span.label: the detuned oscillators model - a place cell oscillates slightly faster than theta, the two shift apart from a common start, and because the cell fires at the peaks of its own membrane potential oscillation this occurs earlier and earlier relative to theta
span.quote: The detuned oscillators model was originally proposed by O'Keefe and Recce ( 1993 ) in their initial report of phase precession, and remains one of the most elegant hypotheses to date 1 ( Figure 3A ). This model considers a place cell that oscillates at a slightly faster frequency than theta. These two oscillators, synchronized at the beginning of the place field, slowly shift due to their frequency difference. Because the place cell fires at the peaks of its own membrane potential oscillation, i.e., its more depolarized states, this occurs earlier and earlier relative to the slower theta oscillation, which results in phase precession.

span.label: somato-dendritic interference - the timing of action potentials is set by oscillatory somatic inhibition combined with ramp-like dendritic excitation, so the cell fires when excitation overcomes inhibition, earlier and earlier because the ramp rises
span.quote: Somato-dendritic interference models ( Figure 3B ; Kamondi et al., 1998 ; Magee, 2001 ; Harris et al., 2002 ; Mehta et al., 2002 ; Losonczy et al., 2010 ) posit that the timing of action potentials is determined by the combination of oscillatory somatic inhibition and transient ramp-like dendritic excitation. As the animal enters the place field, the cell fires when excitation overcomes inhibition, which occurs earlier and earlier because of the ramp-like shape of the dendritic depolarization.

span.label: network connectivity - phase precession results from transmission delays between asymmetrically connected cells, with the delays shortening as the animal progresses through the field
span.quote: In the network connectivity models , contrary to the above cellular models in which no particular synaptic connectivity is assumed, phase precession results from transmission delays between asymmetrically connected cells ( Figure 3C ; Jensen and Lisman, 1996 ; Skaggs et al., 1996 ; Tsodyks et al., 1996 ; Romani and Tsodyks, 2015 ). According to these models, place cells are unidirectional and asymmetrically connected to each other. Feed-forward sensory inputs arriving when the animal reaches the end of the place field drive the cells to fire at early phases of the theta oscillation. Activity then spreads to place cells with fields located further along the trajectory (via asymmetric connections), which fire later in the cycle due to transmission delays. Hence, place cells fire earlier and earlier as the animal progresses through their field, resulting in phase precession.

span.label: and the theta-gamma code, in which the number of nested gamma cycles per theta cycle sets how many items can be represented, related to the seven plus or minus two items humans can hold in short term memory
span.quote: This would enable the hippocampal network to represent four to eight items per theta cycle (corresponding to the number of nested gamma cycles), which has been related (Lisman and Idiart, 1995 ) to the “magic number” of 7 ± 2 items that humans can typically hold in short term memory (Miller, 1956 ).

span.label: The review cannot resolve which functions belong to theta sequences, to awake replay, or to both.
span.quote: Thus, it remains currently unclear which specific functions are sustained by theta sequences, awake replay, or both.

span.label: In the authors' own key experiment the functional role of theta sequences was inferred from network patterns rather than measured behaviorally.
span.quote: Note that in this study, the functional role of theta sequences was not assessed from behavior (task performance), but from the occurrence of dynamic network patterns with a well-documented function, namely trajectory replay underlying memory consolidation.

span.label: no model appears to fully account for all aspects of phase precession
span.quote: While no model appears to fully account for all aspects of phase precession, a continued dialogue between experimental and modeling approaches has provided constraints on potential generation mechanisms.

span.label: and it becomes unclear whether intracellular data do discriminate between different classes of models of phase precession, because the same recordings support two of them and a third can account for the same findings
span.quote: While this supports the somato-dentritic interference models, the same studies also reported that spikes remain locked to the peaks of the membrane potential, a critical prediction of the detuned oscillators models. And because recent work has shown that even network connectivity models (see below) can account for these findings (Romani and Tsodyks, 2015 ), it becomes unclear whether intracellular data do discriminate between different classes of models of phase precession.

span.label: only three studies have reported task performance deficits linked to a degradation of theta sequences, because interfering with theta sequences is challenging
span.quote: Because the mechanisms underlying theta sequences remain poorly understood and may involve many interacting factors (including single-cell properties, synaptic connectivity patterns, local inhibition, theta-paced inputs, etc.), interfering with theta sequences is challenging. To the best of our knowledge, only three studies have reported task performance deficits linked to a degradation of theta sequences.

span.label: and an alternative possibility is that these performance deficits resulted from impairments in planning and decision making rather than from deterioration of learning and memory processes
span.quote: Yet, an alternative possibility is that these performance deficits resulted from impairments in planning and decision making, which also appear to involve theta sequences (Johnson et al., 2007 ; Schmidt et al., 2013 ; Wikenheiser and Redish, 2015b ; Amemiya and Redish, 2016 ), rather than from deterioration of learning and memory processes.

span.label: network connectivity models are difficult to reconcile with the finding that the relation between phase and allocentric position changes during backward movement, and that this change occurs abruptly
span.quote: In both cases, the proposed mechanisms are difficult to reconcile with the experimental finding that the relation between phase and allocentric spatial position changes during backward movement (Cei et al., 2014 ; Maurer et al., 2014 ). Further, this change occurs abruptly, ruling out the possibility that asymmetry could reverse via slow plasticity processes

span.label: the model requires neurons with cosine directional tuning, and although similar cells were documented in entorhinal cortex the finding remains controversial
span.quote: The model requires neurons with cosine directional tuning, which have been identified in the hippocampus, medial septum and anterior thalamus (Welday et al., 2011 ). Similar cells were documented in entorhinal cortex (Krupic et al., 2012 ), although the finding remains controversial (Krupic et al., 2015 ; Navratilova et al., 2016 ).

span.label: the magic number of seven plus or minus two items, related to the number of nested gamma cycles a theta cycle can hold
span.quote: This would enable the hippocampal network to represent four to eight items per theta cycle (corresponding to the number of nested gamma cycles), which has been related (Lisman and Idiart, 1995 ) to the “magic number” of 7 ± 2 items that humans can typically hold in short term memory (Miller, 1956 ).

span.label: the argument that robust activation patterns can be detected without access to the fine time scale of neuronal computation, carried over to tagged-ensemble experiments
span.quote: A parallel can be made with fRMI studies showing robust and consistent activation patterns in response to similar stimuli, despite the low temporal and spatial resolution of the technique (Guest and Love, 2017 ). Thus, while certain types of computation can still be detected or elicited even without having access to the fine time scale of neuronal computation, it is uncertain that they reflect actual brain computation during learning and memory.

span.label: two oscillators of slightly different frequency drifting apart from a common start, used as the original model of phase precession
span.quote: The detuned oscillators model was originally proposed by O'Keefe and Recce ( 1993 ) in their initial report of phase precession, and remains one of the most elegant hypotheses to date 1 ( Figure 3A ). This model considers a place cell that oscillates at a slightly faster frequency than theta. These two oscillators, synchronized at the beginning of the place field, slowly shift due to their frequency difference. Because the place cell fires at the peaks of its own membrane potential oscillation, i.e., its more depolarized states, this occurs earlier and earlier relative to the slower theta oscillation, which results in phase precession.

span.label: transmission delays through an asymmetrically connected chain, used to produce phase precession without any assumption about single-cell oscillation
span.quote: In the network connectivity models , contrary to the above cellular models in which no particular synaptic connectivity is assumed, phase precession results from transmission delays between asymmetrically connected cells ( Figure 3C ; Jensen and Lisman, 1996 ; Skaggs et al., 1996 ; Tsodyks et al., 1996 ; Romani and Tsodyks, 2015 ). According to these models, place cells are unidirectional and asymmetrically connected to each other. Feed-forward sensory inputs arriving when the animal reaches the end of the place field drive the cells to fire at early phases of the theta oscillation. Activity then spreads to place cells with fields located further along the trajectory (via asymmetric connections), which fire later in the cycle due to transmission delays. Hence, place cells fire earlier and earlier as the animal progresses through their field, resulting in phase precession.

span.label: time jitter added to experimental spike trains
span.quote: Several studies have challenged the idea that phase precession could entirely account for theta sequences, by showing that a moderate addition of time jitter to experimental spike trains resulted in preservation of phase precession but a reduced prevalence of theta sequences (Dragoi and Buzsáki, 2006 ; Foster and Wilson, 2007 ; Itskov et al., 2008 ). This suggested that theta sequences required precise coordination between cell assemblies in addition to independent phase precession mechanisms.

span.label: travel direction and running speed taken into account before asking whether peer cells improve prediction
span.quote: To formally test the requirement for additional coordination mechanisms, Chadwick et al. ( 2015 ) developed phenomenological models of independent and coordinated place cell activity during navigation, and compared their predictions in light of experimental data. They concluded that the independent coding model is sufficient to replicate the data previously interpreted as evidence for the coordinated assembly hypothesis.

span.label: a treadmill switched on or off during passive travel, which impairs phase precession while leaving the spatial layout of place fields intact
span.quote: We have recently leveraged this protocol to selectively impair phase precession (treadmill off) or leave it intact (treadmill on), while maintaining the spatial layout of place fields in the environment (Drieu et al., 2018 ). The rats were tested in an entirely novel environment, to stimulate spatial learning, network coordination and synaptic plasticity (Li et al., 2003 ; Leutgeb et al., 2004 ; Cheng and Frank, 2008 ; O'Neill et al., 2008 ), as well as to ensure that previously formed memory traces would not bias our observations. As expected, impaired phase precession during passive travel (treadmill off) was accompanied by an almost complete absence of theta sequences. On the other hand, behavioral timescale sequences were unaffected. During subsequent sleep, the hippocampal network failed to replay trajectories. Only following “active” travel (treadmill on), when theta sequences emerged nested within behavioral timescale sequences, did the hippocampal network generate genuine replay events during sleep (Drieu et al., 2018 ) ( Figure 6C ). This indicates that theta sequences play a causal role in establishing initial memory traces, which can later be reinstated during sleep for memory consolidation.

span.label: the functional readout taken from network patterns rather than from task performance
span.quote: Note that in this study, the functional role of theta sequences was not assessed from behavior (task performance), but from the occurrence of dynamic network patterns with a well-documented function, namely trajectory replay underlying memory consolidation. As a consequence, this alleviates the ambiguity discussed earlier, that behavioral impairments could result either from memory deficits, or from impairments in planning and decision making.

span.label: theta sequence
span.quote: Several studies have challenged the idea that phase precession could entirely account for theta sequences, by showing that a moderate addition of time jitter to experimental spike trains resulted in preservation of phase precession but a reduced prevalence of theta sequences (Dragoi and Buzsáki, 2006 ; Foster and Wilson, 2007 ; Itskov et al., 2008 ). This suggested that theta sequences required precise coordination between cell assemblies in addition to independent phase precession mechanisms.

span.label: jitter
span.quote: Several studies have challenged the idea that phase precession could entirely account for theta sequences, by showing that a moderate addition of time jitter to experimental spike trains resulted in preservation of phase precession but a reduced prevalence of theta sequences (Dragoi and Buzsáki, 2006 ; Foster and Wilson, 2007 ; Itskov et al., 2008 ). This suggested that theta sequences required precise coordination between cell assemblies in addition to independent phase precession mechanisms.

span.label: muscimol
span.quote: medial septum inactivation by muscimol injection abolished theta sequences both on the maze and in the wheel where the rats ran during delay periods (although measures of theta cycles and therefore theta sequences may not be as reliable when theta amplitude vanishes following muscimol injection).

span.label: Theta sequences → synaptic plasticity
span.note: ENABLING, NOT CAUSING, AND THE OTHER WAY ROUND: theta sequences chunk information into time windows CONDUCIVE TO classical synaptic plasticity mechanisms. `causes` overstates 'conducive to', and the retracted edge also had it backwards.
span.quote: While initial reports emphasized the presence of sequential activity during single theta cycles, recent studies have increasingly recognized that a notable fraction of theta cycles contain non-canonical activity, including seemingly random noise and even reverse sequences. Theta sequences chunk information into time windows conducive to classical synaptic plasticity mechanisms, and appear to support the initial storage of memory traces. Within familiar environments, theta sequences allow the maintenance (and possibly the update) of planned trajectories in working memory. During VTE, extended neuronal sweeps may support deliberative processes. Awake replay could also support trajectory planning, on-line consolidation and reconsolidation, as well as on-line retrieval of long-term memory. Thus, it remains currently unclear which specific functions are sustained by theta sequences, awake replay, or both.

span.label: THE PAPER SHIPS ITS OWN GLOSSARY, AND THE FIRST ENTRY LEAVES A PROPERTY UNDETERMINED: a cell assembly is a group of neurons that transiently co-activate, and RECIPROCAL CONNECTIVITY BETWEEN GROUP MEMBERS MAY OR MAY NOT BE IMPLIED
span.quote: Cell assembly. Group of neurons that transiently co-activate during a certain function or mental process. Place cells with highly similar fields can fire within a brief window of time (common theta phase, often grouped within a gamma cycle) and form a cell assembly. Reciprocal connectivity between group members may or may not be implied (e.g., cell assemblies in CA3 vs. CA1).

span.label: with the central term defined by an example and a number: a theta sequence is the sequential activation of cell assemblies paced by the ongoing theta rhythm, representing the ongoing trajectory AT A HIGHLY ACCELERATED RATE - a second of running compressed into about 150 ms
span.quote: Theta sequence. Sequential activation of hippocampal cell assemblies paced by the ongoing theta rhythm (~8 Hz) and representing the ongoing trajectory at a highly accelerated rate. For instance, when a rat successively traverses place fields A, B, and C (which lasts on the order of a second), in the overlapping region, ongoing theta cycles contain spikes A, B, and C in the same order (within only ~150 ms). Theta sequences typically span one theta cycle, but longer sequences have also been described.

span.label: and the definition of replay carries the fact that later spoiled the tidy story - replay CAN OCCUR BOTH IN THE FORWARD OR BACKWARD DIRECTION
span.quote: Replay. Reinstatement during offline states of the sequential activity observed during behavior. Replay is associated with sharp wave ripple complexes and can occur both in the forward or backward direction.

span.label: the definition of phase precession is extended past its original object: initially described in place cells, it has also been reported in interneurons, episode and sound-responsive cells, IN WHICH CASE THE MOVEMENT IS CONSIDERED IN A MORE ABSTRACT SPACE
span.quote: Theta phase precession. The time at which a cell fires relative to the ongoing theta cycle (“phase”) decreases as the animal moves through space. Thus, the cell initially fires at the end of a theta cycle, then slightly before the end of the next cycle, until it eventually fires its last spikes near the beginning of the ongoing theta cycle. This phenomenon is called “phase precession.” Initially described in place cells, phase precession has also been reported in other hippocampal cells, including interneurons, “episode,” and sound-responsive cells (in which case the movement is considered in a more abstract space), as well as in other brain structures such as the medial prefrontal cortex or the ventral striatum.

span.label: and nested sequences are defined as the same assemblies doing two things at once - behavioral sequences in real time, and theta sequences describing the same trajectory nested within them
span.quote: Nested sequences. As a rat explores an environment, place cell assemblies activate in sequence and thus form “behavioral” (slow time scale) sequences representing the ongoing trajectory in real time. Simultaneously, the same assemblies form theta (fast time scale) sequences that describe the same trajectory, nested within the behavioral sequences.

span.label: A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO OTHER PAPERS, WITH THE PARAMETER IT TURNS ON, STATED BY A THIRD: the apparent inconsistency with the results of one study MAY STEM FROM THE LIMITED NUMBER OF REPLAY EVENTS EXAMINED in the other
span.quote: The balance between replay and preplay may also depend on task contingencies, as Ólafsdóttir et al. ( 2017 ) found a greater proportion of forward replay immediately (< 5 s) before and after movement or during short stops (< 10 s), but no directional bias during longer periods of immobility (although one cannot exclude that the apparent inconsistency with the results of Diba and Buzsáki ( 2007 ) may stem from the limited number of replay events examined in the Ólafsdóttir et al. ( 2017 ) study).

span.label: THE DATA CANNOT SEPARATE THE THEORIES, SAID PLAINLY: the same studies support the interference models and also report the critical prediction of the rival models, and because a third class can account for the same findings IT BECOMES UNCLEAR WHETHER INTRACELLULAR DATA DO DISCRIMINATE between different classes of models
span.quote: While this supports the somato-dentritic interference models, the same studies also reported that spikes remain locked to the peaks of the membrane potential, a critical prediction of the detuned oscillators models. And because recent work has shown that even network connectivity models (see below) can account for these findings (Romani and Tsodyks, 2015 ), it becomes unclear whether intracellular data do discriminate between different classes of models of phase precession.

span.label: with the question itself left open: WHETHER PHASE PRECESSION IS A CAUSE OR A CONSEQUENCE of the formation of theta sequences REMAINS UNRESOLVED - and both readings are spelled out, one where precession causes sequences and one where it is their single-cell manifestation
span.quote: Whether phase precession is a cause or a consequence of the formation of theta sequences remains unresolved. As discussed above, phase precession could result from a variety of mechanisms that do not require sequential connectivity between neighboring place cells ( detuned oscillators and somato-dendritic interference models). Independent initiation of phase precession in successive cells would automatically yield theta sequences (Skaggs et al., 1996 ). Thus, phase precession would be a causal mechanism of theta sequences. An alternative view is that hippocampal sequences result from specific patterns of connectivity within the hippocampal network ( network connectivity models; see also Dragoi and Tonegawa, 2011 ). At the single cell level, this would be manifested as phase precessing spikes. Thus, phase precession would be a consequence of the formation of theta sequences.

span.label: A REINTERPRETATION THAT REMOVES EVIDENCE FROM A HYPOTHESIS WITHOUT NEW DATA: the independent coding model IS SUFFICIENT TO REPLICATE THE DATA PREVIOUSLY INTERPRETED AS EVIDENCE FOR THE COORDINATED ASSEMBLY HYPOTHESIS
span.quote: To formally test the requirement for additional coordination mechanisms, Chadwick et al. ( 2015 ) developed phenomenological models of independent and coordinated place cell activity during navigation, and compared their predictions in light of experimental data. They concluded that the independent coding model is sufficient to replicate the data previously interpreted as evidence for the coordinated assembly hypothesis.

span.label: and the reversal is quantitative, not rhetorical - once travel direction and running speed are taken into account, PEER INFORMATION EVEN DECREASES THE AVERAGE PREDICTION
span.quote: As a matter of fact, peer information even decreases the average prediction, consistent with the independent coding model.

span.label: ONE FINDING UNDERMINING A WHOLE FRAMEWORK: a novel form of synaptic potentiation at the behavioral timescale could store entire sequences of events seconds before and after, which EFFECTIVELY UNDERMINES THE THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK that theta sequences are REQUIRED to bring spike trains into temporal proximity
span.quote: Bittner et al. ( 2017 ) recently uncovered a novel form of synaptic potentiation occurring at the behavioral timescale, and proposed that this could suffice to store entire sequences of events that took place several seconds before and after initiation of plateau-potentials in CA1 pyramidal cells. This effectively undermines the theoretical framework that theta sequences are required to bring spike trains in close temporal proximity and enable synaptic potentiation, underlying hippocampus-dependent memory encoding.

span.label: THREE CAUSAL STUDIES, THREE CONFOUNDS SUPPLIED BY THE REVIEWERS RATHER THAN BY THE ORIGINAL AUTHORS. First: the drug that impaired the task also DECREASES RIPPLE POWER, so the deficit could come from altered activity during awake ripples instead
span.quote: One potential caveat however is that CP55940 administration decreases ripple power (Robbe et al., 2006 ). Since place cell activity during awake ripples may play a crucial role in working memory (Jadhav et al., 2012 ), it is conceivable that the performance deficit could also result from altered place cell activity during awake ripples.

span.label: second: one cannot entirely rule out that the deficits were DIRECTLY DUE TO DISRUPTION OF THETA OSCILLATIONS, given an 80% decrease in theta power
span.quote: One cannot entirely rule out that the observed performance deficits could be directly due to disruption of theta oscillations (Pan and McNaughton, 1997 ; Hasselmo et al., 2002 ) induced by medial septum inactivation (~80% decrease in theta power, Wang et al., 2015 ).

span.label: and third, a measurement caveat that undercuts the measurement itself - measures of theta cycles AND THEREFORE THETA SEQUENCES MAY NOT BE AS RELIABLE WHEN THETA AMPLITUDE VANISHES following the injection that produced the effect
span.quote: medial septum inactivation by muscimol injection abolished theta sequences both on the maze and in the wheel where the rats ran during delay periods (although measures of theta cycles and therefore theta sequences may not be as reliable when theta amplitude vanishes following muscimol injection).

span.label: with the size of the evidence base stated: ONLY THREE STUDIES have reported task performance deficits linked to a degradation of theta sequences, because interfering with theta sequences is challenging
span.quote: Because the mechanisms underlying theta sequences remain poorly understood and may involve many interacting factors (including single-cell properties, synaptic connectivity patterns, local inhibition, theta-paced inputs, etc.), interfering with theta sequences is challenging. To the best of our knowledge, only three studies have reported task performance deficits linked to a degradation of theta sequences.

span.label: A CLAIM WITH NO CITABLE SOURCE, INSIDE A PEER-REVIEWED REVIEW: a small fraction of theta cycles do contain significant reverse theta sequences, cited to two papers AND OUR OWN UNPUBLISHED OBSERVATIONS - and the next sentence says the function of reverse theta sequences REMAINS UNCLEAR
span.quote: Yet, a small fraction of theta cycles do contain significant reverse theta sequences (Gupta et al., 2012 ; Zheng et al., 2016 ; our own unpublished observations). The function of reverse theta sequences remains unclear.

span.label: and a fact reported as having been missed rather than absent: ALTHOUGH THIS HAS BEEN OVERLOOKED in initial descriptions of sleep replay, recent studies have reported ABUNDANT REVERSE REPLAY during sleep as well - which DIMS THE USUAL THEORETICAL DISTINCTION between forward theta sequences for encoding, reverse awake replay for goal learning and forward sleep replay for consolidation
span.quote: Similarly, although this has been overlooked in initial descriptions of sleep replay, recent studies have reported abundant reverse replay during sleep as well (Wikenheiser and Redish, 2013 ; Silva et al., 2015 ; Grosmark and Buzsáki, 2016 ; Ólafsdóttir et al., 2016 ; O'Neill et al., 2017 ; Drieu et al., 2018 ). Again, these considerations dim the usual theoretical distinction between (forward) theta sequences for memory encoding, (reverse) awake replay for goal learning, and (forward) sleep replay for memory consolidation.

span.label: A WHOLE TECHNIQUE CRITICISED ON TIMING GROUNDS: tagging studies ARTIFICIALLY ACTIVATE NEURONS IN A HYPER-SYNCHRONOUS MANNER and NEGLECT ANY FINE-TIMESCALE TEMPORAL INFORMATION, and because the labeling window RANGES FROM SEVERAL HOURS TO DAYS the tagged population is likely to include numerous irrelevant neurons
span.quote: One important issue with most of these studies is that they artificially activate neurons in a hyper-synchronous manner, and neglect any fine-timescale temporal information embedded in endogenous spiking patterns. In addition, because the time window for genetic labeling of neuronal networks ranges from several hours to days, the tagged population is likely to include both memory-specific neurons as well as numerous irrelevant neurons that were activated by unrelated events during the relatively long labeling time window. In any case, it remains unclear whether the tagged neurons represent a memory trace or constitute relays toward the relevant ensembles.

span.label: with the same argument extended by analogy - robust activation patterns can be detected WITHOUT HAVING ACCESS TO THE FINE TIME SCALE of neuronal computation, and it is UNCERTAIN THAT THEY REFLECT ACTUAL BRAIN COMPUTATION during learning and memory
span.quote: A parallel can be made with fRMI studies showing robust and consistent activation patterns in response to similar stimuli, despite the low temporal and spatial resolution of the technique (Guest and Love, 2017 ). Thus, while certain types of computation can still be detected or elicited even without having access to the fine time scale of neuronal computation, it is uncertain that they reflect actual brain computation during learning and memory.

span.label: A NUMBER THAT LOOKS LIKE 360 DEGREES ONLY BECAUSE OF POOLING: the range may APPEAR TO SPAN AS MUCH AS 360 degrees WHEN POOLING DATA OVER MULTIPLE FIELD CROSSINGS, while single-trial phase range is typically about 180 and NEVER EXCEEDS A FULL CYCLE
span.quote: While the range over which spike theta phase precesses may appear to span as much as 360° when pooling data over multiple field crossings, single-trial phase range is typically ~180°, and never exceeds a full cycle

span.label: and what the phase codes for is revised by one experiment - the reversal during backward travel INDICATES THAT PHASE DOES NOT CODE FOR THE ALLOCENTRIC POSITION of the animal, BUT MORE LIKELY FOR THE DISTANCE TRAVELED through the field
span.quote: Similarly, the reversal of the phase-position relation observed during backward travel (Cei et al., 2014 ; Maurer et al., 2014 ) indicates that phase does not code for the allocentric position of the animal, but more likely for the distance traveled through the field.

span.label: and then past space altogether: phase precession MAY NOT BE UNIQUELY LINKED TO SPACE, but rather to the full episodic component of the ongoing experience
span.quote: This suggests that phase precession may not be uniquely linked to space, but rather to the full episodic component of the ongoing experience (e.g., reviewed in Jaramillo and Kempter, 2017 ).

span.label: AN EXPECTED TEST THAT WAS NEVER RUN, NAMED AS SUCH: a similar dissociation would be expected in an earlier study - UNFORTUNATELY, THIS WAS NOT INVESTIGATED
span.quote: A similar dissociation would be expected in the study of Gupta et al. ( 2012 ), where theta sequences representing trajectories ahead of the animal, reflecting memory retrieval, could be linked to higher gamma S band power, whereas trajectories behind the animal, reflecting memory encoding, could be linked to higher gamma M band power. Unfortunately, this was not investigated, but two recent studies reported a similar dissociation in rats running on a linear track.

span.label: and a prediction credited in a footnote, retrospectively: in its UNCORRECTED version, this model PREDICTED THAT PLACE CELLS SHOULD FIRE IN REGULAR SPATIAL PATTERNS LONG BEFORE THE DISCOVERY OF GRID CELLS
span.quote: Incidentally, in its “uncorrected” version, this model predicted that place cells should fire in regular spatial patterns long before the discovery of grid cells (see e.g., Lengyel et al. ( 2003 ) for an influential model which eliminates repeated fields).

span.label: THE CONCLUSION KEEPS THE QUESTION OPEN: a notable fraction of theta cycles CONTAIN NON-CANONICAL ACTIVITY, INCLUDING SEEMINGLY RANDOM NOISE AND EVEN REVERSE SEQUENCES, and IT REMAINS CURRENTLY UNCLEAR WHICH SPECIFIC FUNCTIONS ARE SUSTAINED BY THETA SEQUENCES, AWAKE REPLAY, OR BOTH
span.quote: While initial reports emphasized the presence of sequential activity during single theta cycles, recent studies have increasingly recognized that a notable fraction of theta cycles contain non-canonical activity, including seemingly random noise and even reverse sequences. Theta sequences chunk information into time windows conducive to classical synaptic plasticity mechanisms, and appear to support the initial storage of memory traces. Within familiar environments, theta sequences allow the maintenance (and possibly the update) of planned trajectories in working memory. During VTE, extended neuronal sweeps may support deliberative processes. Awake replay could also support trajectory planning, on-line consolidation and reconsolidation, as well as on-line retrieval of long-term memory. Thus, it remains currently unclear which specific functions are sustained by theta sequences, awake replay, or both.

span.label: builds-on → Drieu et al., 2018 (the authors' own treadmill/passive-travel study)
span.quote: We have recently leveraged this protocol to selectively impair phase precession (treadmill off) or leave it intact (treadmill on), while maintaining the spatial layout of place fields in the environment (Drieu et al., 2018 ).

span.label: builds-on → Cei et al., 2014
span.quote: Our previous work has established that passive travel alters phase precession in most place cells (see also Song et al., 2005a ; Terrazas et al., 2005 ), except if the rats actively run on a treadmill while being transported (Cei et al., 2014 ).

span.label: critiques → the usual theoretical distinction between forward theta sequences for encoding, reverse awake replay for goal learning and forward sleep replay for consolidation
span.note: differs in: reverse replay during sleep, overlooked in the initial descriptions and reported abundantly since
span.quote: Similarly, although this has been overlooked in initial descriptions of sleep replay, recent studies have reported abundant reverse replay during sleep as well (Wikenheiser and Redish, 2013 ; Silva et al., 2015 ; Grosmark and Buzsáki, 2016 ; Ólafsdóttir et al., 2016 ; O'Neill et al., 2017 ; Drieu et al., 2018 ). Again, these considerations dim the usual theoretical distinction between (forward) theta sequences for memory encoding, (reverse) awake replay for goal learning, and (forward) sleep replay for memory consolidation.

span.quote: Theta phase precession. The time at which a cell fires relative to the ongoing theta cycle (“phase”) decreases as the animal moves through space. span.quote: Another notable difference between theta sequences and awake replay is that theta sequences seem to be restricted to short distances always encompassing current location, occasionally extending to further locations (Johnson et al., 2007 ; Wikenheiser and Redish, 2015b ), whereas awake replay can span much longer distances (up to ≥10 m; Davidson et al., 2009 ) and be decoupled from current experience (Karlsson and Frank, 2009 ; Gupta et al., 2010 ).

span.quote: While initial reports emphasized the presence of sequential activity during single theta cycles, recent studies have increasingly recognized that a notable fraction of theta cycles contain non-canonical activity, including seemingly random noise and even reverse sequences.

span.label: WHETHER PHASE PRECESSION IS A CAUSE OR A CONSEQUENCE of the formation of theta sequences REMAINS UNRESOLVED
span.quote: Whether phase precession is a cause or a consequence of the formation of theta sequences remains unresolved. As discussed above, phase precession could result from a variety of mechanisms that do not require sequential connectivity between neighboring place cells ( detuned oscillators and somato-dendritic interference models). Independent initiation of phase precession in successive cells would automatically yield theta sequences (Skaggs et al., 1996 ). Thus, phase precession would be a causal mechanism of theta sequences. An alternative view is that hippocampal sequences result from specific patterns of connectivity within the hippocampal network ( network connectivity models; see also Dragoi and Tonegawa, 2011 ). At the single cell level, this would be manifested as phase precessing spikes. Thus, phase precession would be a consequence of the formation of theta sequences.

span.label: NO MODEL APPEARS TO FULLY ACCOUNT FOR ALL ASPECTS of phase precession
span.quote: While no model appears to fully account for all aspects of phase precession, a continued dialogue between experimental and modeling approaches has provided constraints on potential generation mechanisms.

span.label: IT BECOMES UNCLEAR WHETHER INTRACELLULAR DATA DO DISCRIMINATE between different classes of models of phase precession
span.quote: While this supports the somato-dentritic interference models, the same studies also reported that spikes remain locked to the peaks of the membrane potential, a critical prediction of the detuned oscillators models. span.quote: While initial reports emphasized the presence of sequential activity during single theta cycles, recent studies have increasingly recognized that a notable fraction of theta cycles contain non-canonical activity, including seemingly random noise and even reverse sequences. Theta sequences chunk information into time windows conducive to classical synaptic plasticity mechanisms, and appear to support the initial storage of memory traces. Within familiar environments, theta sequences allow the maintenance (and possibly the update) of planned trajectories in working memory. During VTE, extended neuronal sweeps may support deliberative processes. Awake replay could also support trajectory planning, on-line consolidation and reconsolidation, as well as on-line retrieval of long-term memory. Thus, it remains currently unclear which specific functions are sustained by theta sequences, awake replay, or both.

span.label: cell assembly
span.quote: Group of neurons that transiently co-activate during a certain function or mental process.

span.label: theta sequence
span.quote: Sequential activation of hippocampal cell assemblies paced by the ongoing theta rhythm (~8 Hz) and representing the ongoing trajectory at a highly accelerated rate.

span.label: replay
span.quote: Reinstatement during offline states of the sequential activity observed during behavior.

span.label: theta phase precession
span.quote: The time at which a cell fires relative to the ongoing theta cycle (“phase”) decreases as the animal moves through space.

span.label: nested oscillations
span.quote: Intermingled oscillations of different frequencies, especially when the phase of the slower oscillation modulates the amplitude of the faster oscillation.

span.label: nested (behavioral vs theta timescale) sequences
span.quote: As a rat explores an environment, place cell assemblies activate in sequence and thus form “behavioral” (slow time scale) sequences representing the ongoing trajectory in real time.

span.label: vicarious trial and error (VTE)
span.quote: This process is referred to as “vicarious trial and error” (VTE; Muenzinger and Gentry, 1931 ).

span.label: cell assemblies
span.quote: Cell assembly. Group of neurons that transiently co-activate during a certain function or mental process. Place cells with highly similar fields can fire within a brief window of time (common theta phase, often grouped within a gamma cycle) and form a cell assembly. Reciprocal connectivity between group members may or may not be implied (e.g., cell assemblies in CA3 vs. CA1).

span.label: theta sequence
span.quote: Theta sequence. Sequential activation of hippocampal cell assemblies paced by the ongoing theta rhythm (~8 Hz) and representing the ongoing trajectory at a highly accelerated rate. For instance, when a rat successively traverses place fields A, B, and C (which lasts on the order of a second), in the overlapping region, ongoing theta cycles contain spikes A, B, and C in the same order (within only ~150 ms). Theta sequences typically span one theta cycle, but longer sequences have also been described.

span.label: replay
span.quote: Replay. Reinstatement during offline states of the sequential activity observed during behavior. Replay is associated with sharp wave ripple complexes and can occur both in the forward or backward direction.

span.label: phase precession
span.quote: Theta phase precession. The time at which a cell fires relative to the ongoing theta cycle (“phase”) decreases as the animal moves through space. Thus, the cell initially fires at the end of a theta cycle, then slightly before the end of the next cycle, until it eventually fires its last spikes near the beginning of the ongoing theta cycle. This phenomenon is called “phase precession.” Initially described in place cells, phase precession has also been reported in other hippocampal cells, including interneurons, “episode,” and sound-responsive cells (in which case the movement is considered in a more abstract space), as well as in other brain structures such as the medial prefrontal cortex or the ventral striatum.

span.label: nested sequences
span.quote: Nested sequences. As a rat explores an environment, place cell assemblies activate in sequence and thus form “behavioral” (slow time scale) sequences representing the ongoing trajectory in real time. Simultaneously, the same assemblies form theta (fast time scale) sequences that describe the same trajectory, nested within the behavioral sequences.

span.label: 7 ± 2 — the short-term-memory item capacity to which the four-to-eight assemblies per theta cycle have been related
span.quote: This would enable the hippocampal network to represent four to eight items per theta cycle (corresponding to the number of nested gamma cycles), which has been related (Lisman and Idiart, 1995 ) to the “magic number” of 7 ± 2 items that humans can typically hold in short term memory (Miller, 1956 ).

span.label: ~180° — typical single-trial range of theta phase over which a place cell precesses

span.label: phase precession

This suggested that theta sequences required precise coordination between cell assemblies in addition to independent phase precession mechanisms.

span.label: theta sequence
span.quote: We have recently leveraged this protocol to selectively impair phase precession (treadmill off) or leave it intact (treadmill on), while maintaining the spatial layout of place fields in the environment (Drieu et al., 2018 ). The rats were tested in an entirely novel environment, to stimulate spatial learning, network coordination and synaptic plasticity (Li et al., 2003 ; Leutgeb et al., 2004 ; Cheng and Frank, 2008 ; O'Neill et al., 2008 ), as well as to ensure that previously formed memory traces would not bias our observations. As expected, impaired phase precession during passive travel (treadmill off) was accompanied by an almost complete absence of theta sequences. On the other hand, behavioral timescale sequences were unaffected. During subsequent sleep, the hippocampal network failed to replay trajectories. Only following “active” travel (treadmill on), when theta sequences emerged nested within behavioral timescale sequences, did the hippocampal network generate genuine replay events during sleep (Drieu et al., 2018 ) ( Figure 6C ). This indicates that theta sequences play a causal role in establishing initial memory traces, which can later be reinstated during sleep for memory consolidation.

span.label: replay
